q: On the Moon the acceleration of free fall is $1.62\,\text{m/s}^2$. What is the speed of a stone dropped from rest after $3.0\,\text{s}$, and how many times greater would the speed be on Earth in the same time?
a: On the Moon $v = gt = 1.62\,\text{m/s}^2 \cdot 3.0\,\text{s} \approx 4.9\,\text{m/s}$. On Earth $v = 9.81\,\text{m/s}^2 \cdot 3.0\,\text{s} \approx 29\,\text{m/s}$. The speed is directly proportional to the acceleration of free fall, so on Earth it is $9.81 : 1.62 \approx 6.1$ times greater.
